rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps

Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer:
You pick the order. Timestamps don't matter here. Walking Ballista's own "enters with X +1/+1 counters" is the event being modified, and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are two replacement effects trying to modify it. Per `616.1`, the affected object's controller (you) chooses which one applies first. Then, per `616.1f`, the other one applies to the modified event. Neither is a self-replacement effect, so `616.1e` lets you choose either one.

With X=2:
• **Hardened Scales** first: 2 → 3, then **Doubling Season**: 3 → **6 counters**.
• Doubling Season first: 2 → 4, then Hardened Scales: 4 → 5 counters.

So put Scales first and you get a 6/6.

Both cards apply to counters a permanent enters with (Scryfall rulings on each), and the Hardened Scales ruling confirms that you choose the order. Each effect applies only once (`614.5`), so there's no loop.

The same choice comes up with Ballista's {4} ability: 1 counter becomes 4 if Scales goes first, or 3 if Doubling Season goes first.

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer:
No. Under **Blood Moon** each Tron land is just a Mountain. **Urza's Tower** taps for {R}, not {C}{C}{C}, and so do **Urza's Mine** and **Urza's Power Plant**. That's 3 red mana in total, not 7 colorless.

Why: Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." That's a type-changing effect, applied in layer 4 per `613.1d`. Per Blood Moon's Scryfall ruling, nonbasic lands "will lose any other land types and abilities they had. They will gain the land type Mountain and gain the ability "{T}: Add {R}.""

So Tower loses its whole printed ability, including the "add {C}{C}{C} instead" part. Even if that ability were still there, it wouldn't work: the Tron abilities check for land types, not names, and the Urza's Mine, Urza's Power-Plant and Urza's Tower subtypes are gone too. The lands keep their names and stay nonbasic, but that doesn't help, since only the land types matter.

To get Tron back, you need to remove Blood Moon.

rows.question: follow up: what if I play [[Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth]] AFTER the moon is already down? urborg has the later timestamp so shouldn't it make everything a Swamp too? my friend says no
rows.expected_answer: Your friend is right. Both effects are layer 4 type-changing effects (613.1d). Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). Urborg is just a Mountain with '{T}: Add {R}' and nothing becomes a Swamp. (Any actual basic Swamps you control are still Swamps because Blood Moon only affects nonbasic lands.)

outcome.answer:
Your friend is right. Playing **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** after **Blood Moon** still makes nothing a Swamp. Urborg is just a Mountain with no other abilities, and timestamps don't change that.

The official Urborg ruling covers this exact case. If a moon effect sets Urborg to a basic land type, "it won't turn lands into Swamps, no matter in what order those effects started to apply."

Why timestamps don't decide it: both effects change types, so both apply in layer 4. Normally effects in the same layer apply in timestamp order. But per `613.8`, "If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system." Under `613.8a`, Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's, because applying Blood Moon would change "the text or the existence of the first effect." Blood Moon ("Nonbasic lands are Mountains.") turns Urborg, a nonbasic land, into a Mountain that loses its other abilities, including "Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types." Blood Moon does not depend on Urborg in return.

So Blood Moon applies first, and per `613.8b` Urborg's effect waits until after it. By then the effect no longer exists, so no land becomes a Swamp. Urborg itself is a legendary nonbasic Mountain that taps for {R} only.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is just a regular **Tarmogoyf**. It doesn't get your counters or the Giant Growth bonus, but it does copy the ability that sets Tarmogoyf's size, so it will be exactly as big as a fresh goyf.

Per `707.2`, a copy takes only the copiable values, meaning the values from the printed text. "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." That means your two +1/+1 counters and **Giant Growth**'s +3/+3 ("Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn") stay with your goyf. The Clone rulings say the same thing: Clone doesn't copy counters or "any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness".

The size isn't a problem. Per `707.2a`, a copy gets the abilities of the object it copies, and that includes Tarmogoyf's text: "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1." The Clone counts the graveyards itself, all the time. The only time a copy loses that ability is when the copy effect sets its own power and toughness, like Quicksilver Gargantuan in `707.9d`. Plain Clone doesn't do that.

For example, if the graveyards hold three card types, their Clone is 3/4. Your goyf is 3/4 + 2 counters + 3 = 8/9 until end of turn. Note that Giant Growth is an instant, so if it's the first instant in any graveyard, both goyfs count it.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
With **Humility** out first and **Opalescence** arriving later, your creatures are still 1/1 with no abilities. Humility becomes a 4/4 enchantment creature with no abilities. Opalescence isn't a creature at all and keeps working. If Opalescence had been out first, Humility would be a 1/1 instead.

Opalescence says "Each other non-Aura enchantment is a creature", so it never animates itself. It stays a noncreature enchantment, and Humility can't touch its ability.

Here's how the layers work out:

Layer 4: Opalescence makes Humility (and any other non-Aura enchantment) a creature.
Layer 6: Humility removes all abilities from all creatures, including itself. Per 613.6, once Humility's effect has started applying, it keeps applying in later layers "even if the ability generating the effect is removed during this process." So Humility still makes things 1/1 in 7b.
Layer 7b: Humility and Opalescence both set base P/T, so they apply in timestamp order (613.4b, 613.7). The later one wins.

Humility first: Humility sets everything to 1/1. Then Opalescence sets Humility to 4/4, its mana value. Any other enchantment creatures end up at their mana value, while normal creatures stay 1/1.
Opalescence first: Opalescence sets Humility to 4/4. Then Humility sets every creature, itself included, to 1/1.

Either way, every creature has no abilities, and creatures that aren't enchantments are 1/1. This matches the official Humility/Opalescence ruling.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes, you can cast **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** straight from your hand for {5}{B}{R}. When you cast a modal double-faced card, you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack (712.11b). On the stack and on the battlefield, it has only the characteristics of the face that's up (712.8f). So it's a Tibalt planeswalker spell, and then a Tibalt planeswalker permanent.

In your library, graveyard, hand or exile, it's **not** a planeswalker card. Outside the stack and battlefield, a double-faced card has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a). There it's just **Valki**, a legendary creature card with mana value 2.

That doesn't matter for your two examples, though. **Vraska's Contempt** reads "Exile target creature or planeswalker" and **Kaya's Ghostform** has "Enchant creature or planeswalker you control". Both only look at permanents on the battlefield. A Tibalt on the battlefield is a legal choice for either one.

One catch: suppose Tibalt has Ghostform on it and gets exiled or dies. Ghostform will "return that card to the battlefield". A double-faced card put onto the battlefield from anywhere other than the stack comes in front face up by default (712.14). So it comes back as Valki, not Tibalt.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?
rows.expected_answer: 1) Yes. Color identity includes mana symbols in the mana cost AND in the rules text (903.4), so Kenrith's identity is WUBRG even though his mana cost is only {4}{W}. Nicol Bolas, the Ravager (UBR) is legal because every color in its identity is in Kenrith's (903.5c). 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead - a replacement effect (903.9b). Graveyard/exile use a separate state-based action (903.9a). Either way it's optional.

outcome.answer:

rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose. The 6 from the **Clone** doesn't count toward Rafiq's commander damage. Noncombat damage like **Fling** never counts either.

Commander status belongs to the physical card, not to its characteristics. Per `903.3`, "A permanent that’s copying a commander (such as a Body Double, for example, copying a commander in a player’s graveyard) is not a commander." The Clone is a perfect copy of **Rafiq of the Many**, but it isn't her commander. Its damage only reduces your life total.

The loss condition in `903.10a` needs 21 or more *combat* damage from the *same* commander. You're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. Keep in mind that Rafiq hands out double strike: "Whenever a creature you control attacks alone, it gains double strike until end of turn." Combined with exalted, Rafiq attacking alone can finish that last 6 quickly.

On Fling: it only says "combat damage", so Fling's damage doesn't count, even if she sacrifices the real Rafiq to it. In that case Fling deals the damage, not the commander, and it isn't combat damage anyway. It still makes you lose life as normal.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?

You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

This is the normal way to cast spells. Floating mana ahead of time works too, but it only lasts until the end of the current step or phase (see answer 1).

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
rows.expected_answer: No copy. Academy Manufactor's "instead" makes it a replacement effect (614.1a), and Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, so Manufactor applies. The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token. Those are predefined tokens with only their standard characteristics (111.10a, 111.10b, 111.10f). 111.10 lets the effect that creates a predefined token modify it, but Shelob's modifications belonged to the replaced event, and Manufactor's own effect modifies nothing. You end up with a plain Food, a plain Clue and a plain Treasure, and the creature is not copied.

outcome.answer:
You get no copy of the creature. **Academy Manufactor** replaces Shelob's token creation. You create one plain Food, one plain Clue and one plain Treasure, and none of them is a copy of the creature that died.

**Shelob, Child of Ungoliant** tries to create a token that is a Food artifact. Manufactor says: "If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each." Because it uses "instead", it is a replacement effect (`614.1a`). Per `614.6`, a replaced event never happens; a modified event happens instead. So the copy-Food creation is thrown out completely. In its place you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure, and those are the standard predefined tokens. Shelob's "copy of that creature" part belonged to the event that got replaced, so none of the three new tokens gets it. "One of each" doesn't mean you keep the original token and add the two missing types.

Since no copy enters, the dead creature's enters-the-battlefield abilities won't trigger either. Each extra Manufactor multiplies the count, as its rulings describe.

I've marked this medium confidence: the Comprehensive Rules don't address this exact pairing directly. The ruling comes from applying Manufactor's replacement as written, together with `614.6`.
